obernants.approximation_semantics: Proposed inner bound of absent behavior under the stated premises; source-derived and checked on finite fixtures, not proved for all Rust executions.
obernants.assumptions: Lawful ordering/cloning where required, standard Rust and successful allocation.
obernants.domain: Finite lawful Ord + Clone arrays and query/update observations, excluding resource failure and panicking user code.
obernants.operator: In the universe of arrays, operations, outputs and successor states, exclude any minimum outside the requested range, nonminimum or nonleftmost ties, Some for invalid/empty ranges, changed state on invalid update, and changes to other points after valid update.

obernants.operator: A returned index j admits arrays with s<=j<e, A[j]<=A[k] for all k in the range, and A[j]<A[k] for k<j. None admits exactly invalid or empty ranges. A post-update array admits all antecedents agreeing outside i; the overwritten value is unconstrained. Invalid update admits only an identical prior state.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived conditional relation with finite executed checks; no unrestricted semantic proof.
obernants.assumptions: Lawful total ordering; value-preserving independent clones where required; source-bound tests; no panics, overflow or allocation failure.
obernants.domain: Finite lawful ordered value arrays, successful allocation, nonpanicking operations; fixed lengths, ranges and transformations as stated.
obernants.observation_scope: Operation observations or finite traces explicitly specified by the relation.
obernants.operator: For fixed A define i meet j = argmin of (A[i],i),(A[j],j), with None as identity. The operation is associative, commutative and idempotent. Q(s,e)=Q(s,m) meet Q(m,e) for 0<=s<=m<=e<=n. Empty pieces are None. This explains why compact tree layout and reduction traversal cannot change tie choices.

obernants.operator: For valid i and range R excluding i, Q(update(A,i,x),R)=Q(A,R), including returned values. At the internal-state level only A[i] and ancestors of leaf n+i may change; unchanged ancestors are allowed. Invalid indices preserve every field. This is not an exception-safety promise for a panicking comparison.

obernants.operator: For distinct valid i,j and fixed replacement values x,y, U(j,y)(U(i,x)(S))=U(i,x)(U(j,y)(S)) as complete deterministic tree states. When i=j equality requires x=y; otherwise the last write wins, so dropping distinctness is false.

obernants.operator: For a fixed length n, observe query(i,i+1) values for every i. The compatible value vector is uniquely A[i]=observed[i]. Rebuilding from A reconstructs the canonical tree, not arbitrary corrupted private state or update history. Observing only singleton indices always yields i and cannot recover values.

obernants.operator: For an order embedding f on the observed value set, Q_f(A)(s,e)=Q_A(s,e): strict comparisons and equalities are preserved. Strictly increasing integer affine maps require no overflow. Merely nondecreasing f is insufficient: [1,0] maps to [0,0], changing index 1 to 0.

obernants.operator: For lawful independent value clones, let C=clone(S). Updates on C leave every query and complete state of S unchanged. Equality after restoring a point uses deterministic canonical construction. Clones with shared interior mutable order state violate the premise and are outside this relation.
